definition_method: Original concise study aids written from the cited KJV passages. No copyrighted commentary wording was imported.

entries.definition: The KJV New Testament form of Jeremiah, the prophet named in Matthew's fulfillment statements. See JEREMIAH.
A name borne by men listed among the captains and people who came to Gedaliah and later approached Jeremiah after Jerusalem's fall.
The KJV New Testament spelling of Jotham, the son of Ozias and father of Achaz in the genealogy of Jesus Christ. See JOTHAM.
The name associated with a family of temple servants listed among those who returned from captivity.
A son or descendant of Javan named in the genealogies of Genesis and Chronicles. See CHITTIM.
LIBNITES, plural noun. A Levitical family descended through Gershon and named among the families of Levi.
LICENCE, noun. Permission, leave, or liberty granted to speak or act.
LUNATICK, noun or adjective. A historical KJV term for a person suffering a recurring severe affliction; Matthew records such sufferers among those Jesus healed.
A duke of Edom named among the chiefs descended from Esau.
MAHLITES, plural noun. A Levitical family belonging to the line of Merari.
MANAHETHITES, plural noun. A family or clan named in the genealogies of Judah in connection with Shobal and Salma.
The parent of Mehetabel and child of Mezahab, named in the record of an Edomite king's family.
The title identified and interpreted in John's Gospel as the Christ.
A name recorded in the sixth priestly course and among the covenant names in Nehemiah.
MORASTHITE, noun or adjective. A person of Moresheth or belonging to it; the designation applied to Micah the prophet.
MUSHITES, plural noun. A Levitical family belonging to the line of Merari and descended from Mushi.
The KJV New Testament spelling of Naphtali, used of the tribal territory named in Matthew's account of Jesus dwelling in Capernaum. See NAPHTALI.
entries.source_title: KJV Bible Place and People Guide

entries.definition: NETOPHATHITES, plural noun. A family or inhabitants associated with Netophah and its villages.
A place in Moab known for its waters, whose desolation is named in prophecies of judgment upon Moab.
The former name of Joshua the son of Nun before Moses called him Jehoshua. See JOSHUA and JEHOSHUA.
